title: Linguistic Features of Local Geometry in Language Models
abstract: Intrinsic dimensionality (ID) describes the effective complexity of language-model representations, but dataset-level estimates obscure variation across individual inputs and make it difficult to examine multiple linguistic properties jointly. We address this limitation by estimating pointwise ID relative to a fixed reference set and relating it to interpretable surface, morphosyntactic, and syntactic features. Across Pythia, Qwen, and Apertus, compact linguistic profiles predict pointwise ID at every analysed depth, with the strongest relationship consistently emerging in intermediate layers. Early-layer geometry is more closely associated with surface properties, whereas nominal composition, pronouns, subject dependencies, and verbal structure become more prominent at intermediate and later depths. These patterns persist across ID estimators, neighbourhood sizes, and controls for input length and lexical frequency. Our findings show that variation in local representation geometry hidden by dataset-level summaries is systematically associated with the linguistic properties of individual inputs.
